args.name: retry-contract
args.task: Author contracts/retry-policy.md as the single authoritative cross-SDK retry contract for the Atlas client SDKs (clients/typescript/client.ts and clients/python/client.py). It must define, precisely enough that two independent implementers produce identical semantics: (1) retryable HTTP statuses = exactly 429 and 503 (state explicitly that other 4xx/5xx, including the 400/500 errors listed in contracts/users.json, are not retried); (2) Retry-After handling — precedence over backoff, accepted formats, units, clamping/invalid-value behavior; (3) exponential backoff — base delay, multiplier, growth formula, jitter policy, and cap; (4) maximum attempts — total-attempt vs retry-count semantics and default value; (5) non-idempotent request protection — which methods/requests are eligible for retry and how a non-idempotent request is protected; (6) behavior when retries are exhausted (error/exception surfaced) and any opt-out/configuration surface. Include a short normalization/conformance table of scenarios (status, headers, method) -> expected attempt counts and delays that both clients must satisfy. Keep it purely client-side: the contract must state that no retry behavior belongs in server/ or web/. Do not implement client code.

args.name: ts-client-retry
args.task: Implement the retry policy specified in contracts/retry-policy.md inside the TypeScript SDK at clients/typescript/client.ts, extending the existing Client class without changing its existing public behavior, and add unit tests (in the location/style used by the repo's existing tests, runnable via `npm test` / node --test) that prove every clause of the contract: only 429 and 503 retried, Retry-After precedence and format handling, exponential backoff values and cap/jitter rules, maximum-attempt accounting, non-idempotent request protection, and exhausted-retry error surfacing. Tests must not require live network or the running server. Report the exact command run and pass/fail counts. Do not modify contracts/retry-policy.md, clients/python/client.py, server/, or web/.

args.name: conformance-review
args.task: Perform an independent joint conformance review of clients/typescript/client.ts and clients/python/client.py against contracts/retry-policy.md, and write the result into tests/sdk-conformance.md (replacing its current placeholder text). For each contract clause, record a reproducible scenario (request method, response status, Retry-After value, expected attempts and delays), the exact command executed in each SDK, the real observed result/exit status, and a per-SDK pass/fail plus a verdict on whether both clients exhibit identical policy semantics. Also confirm no retry behavior was added to server/ or web/. Do not implement fixes. End with exactly one marker: <ACCEPT> if both clients fully conform and the recorded evidence is reproducible; <REVISE> otherwise, followed by a numbered list of specific nonconformities, each tagged TS and/or PY (tag both when the contract wording itself is ambiguous), naming the file and contract clause to correct.
